## Introduction

As Executive Director of the Green Transit Alliance (GTA), this project evaluates the environmental performance of US public transit agencies to determine the winners of the annual GTA Awards. Using data from the National Transit Database (NTD) and Energy Information Administration (EIA), the analysis combines transit ridership, energy consumption, and CO₂ emissions estimates to identify agencies with the highest and lowest emissions efficiency.

### Task 1: 

In this step I collected three datasets to support the analysis. The first contains state-level electricity generation and emissions data from the Energy Information Administration (EIA). The second dataset provides fuel and electricity consumption data for transit agencies from the National Transit Database (NTD). The third contains NTD service data on passenger ridership and miles traveled. 
```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()


```


```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()

```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

### Task 2:
In this step, I cleaned the transit energy dataset by replacing abbreviated transit mode codes with their full descriptive names. This made the data easier to interpret and improved its readability for subsequent analysis.
```{r}

NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(Mode = recode_values(Mode,
    "AR" ~ "Alaska Railroad",
    "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
    "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
    "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
    "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
    "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
    "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
    "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
    "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
    "MB" ~ "Bus",
    "MG" ~ "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
    "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
    "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",

    "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
    "VP" ~ "Vanpool",

  ))
```

### Task 3:
In this step, I conducted exploratory data analysis to identify patterns and trends across the datasets. 

**1. Which 5 states have the most expensive retail electricity?**
```{r}
#| code-fold: true

EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(electricity_price_MWh, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh),
    y = electricity_price_MWh
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "#228B22") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Five States with the Highest Electricity Prices",
    x = "State",
    y = "Electricity Price ($/MWh)",
    caption = "Source: US Energy Information Administration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**2. Which five states have the dirtiest electricity mix?**
```{r}
#| code-fold: true

EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(CO2_MWh, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(state, CO2_MWh, primary_source) |>
  arrange(desc(CO2_MWh)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "State",
      "CO2 Emissions per MWh",
      "Primary Electricity Source"
    ),
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Five States with the Dirtiest Electricity Mix"
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
    full_width = FALSE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::row_spec(
    0,
    background = "#228B22",
    color = "white",
    bold = TRUE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::row_spec(
    c(2, 4),
    background = "#E8F5E9"
  )
```

**3. On average, how many pounds of CO2 are emitted per MWh of electricity produced in the US?**
```{r}
#| code-fold: true

US_Avg_CO2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  summarise(
    avg = weighted.mean(
      CO2_MWh,
      w = generation_MWh,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  pull(avg)

```
On average, approximately `r round(US_Avg_CO2, 2)` pounds of CO₂ are emitted per MWh of electricity generated in the United States.

**5. Texas, has a reputation as being the home of “dirty fossil fuels” while NY has a reputation as a leader in clean energy. How many times cleaner is NY’s energy mix than that of Texas?**
```{r}
#| code-fold: true

NY_TX <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  filter(abbreviation %in% c("NY", "TX")) |>
  select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh)

NY_TX_ratio <- NY_TX |>
  summarise(
    ratio = CO2_MWh[abbreviation == "TX"] /
            CO2_MWh[abbreviation == "NY"]
  ) |>
  pull(ratio)
```

New York's electricity generation mix is approximately
`r round(NY_TX_ratio, 2)` times cleaner than Texas's,
based on CO₂ emissions per MWh of electricity generated.


**6. Which five transit services have the most UPT annually?**
```{r}
#| code-fold: true

NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(AGENCY, mode) |>
  summarise(
    Annual_UPT = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(Annual_UPT, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    Agency_Short = case_when(
      str_detect(AGENCY, "MTA New York City Transit") ~ "MTA NYC Transit",
      str_detect(AGENCY, "Los Angeles County Metropolitan") ~ "LA Metro",
      str_detect(AGENCY, "Chicago Transit Authority") ~ "Chicago CTA",
      str_detect(AGENCY, "Washington Metropolitan") ~ "Washington Metro",
      TRUE ~ AGENCY
    ),
    Mode_Name = case_when(
      mode == "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
      mode == "MB" ~ "Bus",
      TRUE ~ mode
    ),
    Service = paste(Agency_Short, Mode_Name, sep = " - ")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(Service, Annual_UPT),
    y = Annual_UPT
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "forestgreen") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 US Transit Services by Annual Ridership",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Annual Unlinked Passenger Trips (Millions)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)
  )
```

**7. What is the average trip length of a trip on MTA NYC?**
```{r}
#| code-fold: true

MTA_Avg_Trip <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(AGENCY == "MTA New York City Transit") |>
  summarise(
    avg_trip = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE) /

```

The average passenger trip on MTA New York City Transit is approximately `r round(MTA_Avg_Trip, 2)` miles.

**8. Which transit service in NYC has the longest average trip length?**
```{r}
#| code-fold: true

NYC_Longest_Trip <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(city == "New York") |>
  group_by(AGENCY, mode, type_of_service) |>
  summarise(
    Passenger_Miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    UPT = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(UPT > 0) |>
  mutate(
    Avg_Trip_Length = Passenger_Miles / UPT
  ) |>
  slice_max(Avg_Trip_Length, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

The NYC transit service with the longest average passenger trip is `r NYC_Longest_Trip$AGENCY` (`r NYC_Longest_Trip$mode`, `r NYC_Longest_Trip$type_of_service`), with an average trip length of `r round(NYC_Longest_Trip$Avg_Trip_Length, 2)` miles.

### Task 4 & 5

Here, I joined the three datasets to combine transit energy consumption, passenger service information, and state-level electricity emissions data.
```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
service_for_join <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = str_pad(
      as.character(NTD_ID),
      width = 5,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, mode) |>
  summarise(
    AGENCY = first(AGENCY),
    state = first(state),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
energy_for_join <- load_ntd_energy() |>
  rename(
    NTD_ID = `NTD ID`,
    mode = Mode
  ) |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = str_pad(
      as.character(NTD_ID),
      width = 5,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  )

TRANSIT_COMBINED <- energy_for_join |>
  left_join(
    service_for_join,
    by = c("NTD_ID", "mode")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
      select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh),
    by = c("state" = "abbreviation")
  )

TRANSIT_EMISSIONS <- TRANSIT_COMBINED |>
  mutate(
    CO2_Diesel = coalesce(`Gallons of Diesel Fuel`, 0) * 22.45,

    CO2_Gasoline = coalesce(`Gallons of Gasoline`, 0) * 18.73,

    CO2_Kerosene = coalesce(`Gallons of Kerosene`, 0) * 21.78,

    CO2_Bunker = coalesce(`Gallons of Bunker Fuel`, 0) * 24.78,

    CO2_LPG = coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`, 0) * 12.68,

    # Approximate natural gas emissions
    CO2_CNG = coalesce(`Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, 0) * 14.93,

    CO2_LNG = coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`, 0) * 13.5,

    # Approximate biofuel combustion emissions
    CO2_Biodiesel = coalesce(`Gallons of Bio-Diesel`, 0) * 22.45,

    CO2_Ethanol = coalesce(`Gallons of Ethanol`, 0) * 12.7,

    # Hydrogen fuel-cell use produces no direct CO2
    CO2_Hydrogen = 0,

    CO2_Electricity = case_when(
      coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`, 0) +
        coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`, 0) == 0 ~ 0,

      TRUE ~ (
        coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`, 0) +
          coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`, 0)
      ) / 1000 * CO2_MWh
    ),

    Total_CO2_lb = CO2_Diesel +
                   CO2_Gasoline +
                   CO2_Kerosene +
                   CO2_Bunker +
                   CO2_LPG +
                   CO2_CNG +
                   CO2_LNG +
                   CO2_Biodiesel +
                   CO2_Ethanol +
                   CO2_Hydrogen +
                   CO2_Electricity
  )

```

### Task 6

During this phase, I normalized each transit agency's total estimated CO₂ emissions. This allowed for more meaningful comparisons of emissions efficiency across transit agencies of different sizes.
```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
# Step 1: Calculate total emissions by agency
AGENCY_EMISSIONS <- TRANSIT_EMISSIONS |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  summarise(
    AGENCY = first(AGENCY),
    Total_CO2_lb = if (any(is.na(Total_CO2_lb))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      sum(Total_CO2_lb)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Step 2: Calculate total transit usage by agency
AGENCY_USAGE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = str_pad(
      as.character(NTD_ID),
      width = 5,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  summarise(
    Total_UPT = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Passenger_Miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Step 3: Calculate emissions per UPT and passenger mile
AGENCY_EFFICIENCY <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  left_join(AGENCY_USAGE, by = "NTD_ID") |>
  mutate(
    CO2_per_UPT = Total_CO2_lb / Total_UPT,
    CO2_per_Passenger_Mile =
      Total_CO2_lb / Total_Passenger_Miles
  ) |>
  filter(
    Total_UPT > 0,
    Total_Passenger_Miles > 0,
    !is.na(Total_CO2_lb)
  )

library(kableExtra)
library(tidyverse)


# Table 1: Emissions per Passenger Trip
AGENCY_EFFICIENCY |>
  filter(Total_UPT >= 100000, Total_CO2_lb > 0) |>
  arrange(CO2_per_UPT) |>
  select(AGENCY, CO2_per_UPT) |>
  head(10) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    format = "html",
    caption = "Top 10 Most Emissions-Efficient Transit Agencies per Passenger Trip"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  row_spec(0, background = "forestgreen", color = "white", bold = TRUE)


# Table 2: Emissions per Passenger Mile
AGENCY_EFFICIENCY |>
  filter(Total_UPT >= 100000, Total_CO2_lb > 0) |>
  arrange(CO2_per_Passenger_Mile) |>
  select(AGENCY, CO2_per_Passenger_Mile) |>
  head(10) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    format = "html",
    caption = "Top 10 Most Emissions-Efficient Transit Agencies per Passenger Mile"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  row_spec(0, background = "forestgreen", color = "white", bold = TRUE)


# Create dataset for the graph
TOP_10_EFFICIENT <- AGENCY_EFFICIENCY |>
  filter(
    Total_UPT >= 100000,
    Total_CO2_lb > 0,
    !is.na(CO2_per_Passenger_Mile)
  ) |>
  arrange(CO2_per_Passenger_Mile) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(
    Agency_Short = stringr::str_trunc(AGENCY, width = 40)
  )


# Graph: 10 Most Emissions-Efficient Transit Agencies
ggplot(
  TOP_10_EFFICIENT,
  aes(
    x = reorder(Agency_Short, CO2_per_Passenger_Mile),
    y = CO2_per_Passenger_Mile
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#228B22") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "10 Most Emissions-Efficient US Transit Agencies",
    subtitle = "Agencies with at least 100,000 annual passenger boardings",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pounds of CO2 per Passenger Mile",
    caption = "Sources: 2025 NTD and EIA electricity emissions data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
  
### Task 7:

Lastly, I identified the most and least emissions-efficient transit agencies using estimated CO₂ emissions per passenger mile. I compared the winning agencies against the national median to highlight differences in environmental performance and determine the recipients of the GTA Green Transit Awards.
  
  # GTA IV Awards: Recognizing Environmental Performance in US Public Transit

**2025 National Transit Environmental Performance Awards**

The GTA IV Awards recognize environmental performance among US public transit agencies using data from the National Transit Database (NTD) and the US Energy Information Administration (EIA). Agencies were evaluated using estimated carbon dioxide emissions per passenger mile, with eligibility restricted to agencies reporting at least 100,000 annual passenger boardings and positive estimated emissions.

### Award 1: Greenest Transit Agency

**Winner: City of Seattle — Seattle Center Monorail**

Seattle Center Monorail earns the Greenest Transit Agency award with an estimated **0.064 pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile**.

This metric was calculated by dividing each agency's total estimated CO₂ emissions across all transit modes by its total annual passenger miles.

For comparison, the median eligible transit agency produced approximately **1.07 pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile**. Seattle Center Monorail therefore generated approximately **94% less CO₂ per passenger mile than the median agency**, demonstrating exceptional emissions efficiency.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
AWARD_RESULTS <- AGENCY_EFFICIENCY |>
  filter(
    Total_UPT >= 100000,
    Total_CO2_lb > 0,
    is.finite(CO2_per_Passenger_Mile)
  )
GREENEST_CHART <- tibble(
  Agency = c("Seattle Center Monorail", "Median Transit Agency"),
  CO2 = c(
    min(AWARD_RESULTS$CO2_per_Passenger_Mile),
    median(AWARD_RESULTS$CO2_per_Passenger_Mile)
  )
)

ggplot(GREENEST_CHART,
       aes(x = reorder(Agency, -CO2), y = CO2,
           fill = Agency)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", CO2)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Seattle Center Monorail" = "#228B22",
      "Median Transit Agency" = "grey65"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1.25),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Seattle Center Monorail Leads in Emissions Efficiency",
    subtitle = "94% less CO2 per passenger mile than the median transit agency",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pounds of CO2 per Passenger Mile (lower is better)",
    caption = paste(
      "Sources: 2025 National Transit Database (NTD);",
      "US Energy Information Administration (EIA).",
      "\nIncludes agencies with at least 100,000 annual boardings",
      "and positive estimated emissions."
    )
  ) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 25, 15, 15)
  )
```  

### Award 2: Least Emissions-Efficient Transit Agency

**Winner: Plaquemines Port, Harbor and Terminal District — Louisiana Gateway Port**

Louisiana Gateway Port receives the Least Emissions-Efficient Transit Agency award, recording approximately **23.5 pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile**.

This award uses the same emissions-intensity metric as the Greenest Transit Agency award, but identifies the agency with the highest estimated emissions relative to passenger transportation provided.

Compared with the median of **1.07 pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile**, Louisiana Gateway Port produced approximately **22 times more CO₂ per passenger mile**.

Importantly, Louisiana Gateway Port operates ferryboat service, which may help explain its relatively high emissions intensity. Ferry operations can require substantial fuel consumption, particularly when passenger volumes are low. Although the agency recorded significantly higher emissions per passenger mile than the median, this result should be interpreted in the context of its transportation mode and operating conditions. Its ranking does not necessarily indicate poor operational management.
```{r}
#| code-fold: true
WORST_CHART <- tibble(
  Agency = c("Louisiana Gateway Port", "Median Transit Agency"),
  CO2 = c(
    max(AWARD_RESULTS$CO2_per_Passenger_Mile),
    median(AWARD_RESULTS$CO2_per_Passenger_Mile)
  )
)

ggplot(WORST_CHART,
       aes(x = reorder(Agency, CO2), y = CO2,
           fill = Agency)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", CO2)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Louisiana Gateway Port" = "#B85C38",
      "Median Transit Agency" = "grey65"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 27),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Louisiana Gateway Port Has the Highest Emissions Intensity",
    subtitle = "Ferryboat operator emits about 22 times the median CO2 per passenger mile",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pounds of CO2 per Passenger Mile (lower is better)",
    caption = paste(
      "Sources: 2025 National Transit Database (NTD);",
      "US Energy Information Administration (EIA).",
      "\nFerryboat service (FB); comparison includes agencies with",
      "at least 100,000 annual boardings and positive estimated emissions."
    )
  ) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 25, 15, 15)
  )
``` 

### Methodology

Total CO₂ emissions were estimated using reported fuel and electricity consumption, fuel-specific emissions conversion factors, and state-level electricity emissions intensities. Agency emissions were aggregated across transit modes and divided by total annual passenger miles. The median was calculated across eligible agencies using the same filtering criteria.

These awards reflect estimated operational emissions and should not be interpreted as comprehensive lifecycle environmental assessments.
